segments.text: This glass lens is about nine microns thick. This patterned plate is just one micron thick.
segments.say: This glass lens is about nine microns thick. This patterned plate is just one micron thick.

segments.text: Shine green light through both, and they focus it to exactly the same spot.
segments.say: Shine green light through both, and they focus it to exactly the same spot.

segments.text: But in white light, the glass lens still makes one sharp focus, while the plate smears the colours along its axis.
segments.say: But in white light, the glass lens still makes one sharp focus, while the plate smears the colours along its axis.

segments.text: How can one micron of glass do a thick lens's job? And what's the catch?
segments.say: How can one micron of glass do a thick lens's job? And what's the catch?

segments.text: Inside glass, light slows down to c/n, where n, the refractive index, is about 1.5.
segments.say: Inside glass, light slows down, to c over en, where en, the refractive index, is about one point five.

segments.text: Follow two paths, one through a block of glass of height h, one through air. In the glass, the crests bunch up and fall behind.
segments.say: Follow two paths: one through a block of glass of height aitch, one through air. In the glass, the crests bunch up, and fall behind.

segments.text: The glass path lags by (n − 1)h: a phase delay φ = k₀(n − 1)h, where k₀ = 2π/λ.
segments.say: The glass path lags by en minus one, times aitch: a phase delay, phi equals kay naught, times en minus one, times aitch, where kay naught is two pi over lambda.

segments.text: If the glass is thin, each point is simply delayed on its own: the outgoing field is the incoming one, times e^(iφ(x)).
segments.say: If the glass is thin, each point is simply delayed on its own: the outgoing field is the incoming one, times e to the i phi of ex.

segments.text: That's the thin element approximation, TEA. Make the glass thickest in the middle, and a flat wave leaves curved, converging to a focus.
segments.say: That's the thin element approximation, T, E, A. Make the glass thickest in the middle, and a flat wave leaves curved, converging to a focus.

segments.text: It's the simplest, fastest rung on a ladder of models. Remember its one assumption: every point on its own.
segments.say: It's the simplest, fastest rung on a ladder of models. Remember its one assumption: every point, on its own.

segments.text: Now the key trick. Phase is an angle, so a delay of one full turn, 2π, changes nothing: every crest lands where the next one was.
segments.say: Now the key trick. Phase is an angle, so a delay of one full turn, two pi, changes nothing: every crest lands where the next one was.

segments.text: In glass, one full turn of delay takes a height of λ/(n − 1). For green light, that's about 1.1 microns.
segments.say: In glass, one full turn of delay takes a height of lambda over en minus one. For green light, that's about one point one microns.

segments.text: So slice the lens into slabs of exactly that height.
segments.say: So slice the lens into slabs of exactly that height.

segments.text: Each full slab only adds whole turns. It changes nothing, so throw it away.
segments.say: Each full slab only adds whole turns. It changes nothing, so throw it away.

segments.text: Keep just the curved remainders, and let them drop onto the base.
segments.say: Keep just the curved remainders, and let them drop onto the base.

segments.text: What's left is a kinoform: rings called Fresnel zones, about one micron thick.
segments.say: What's left is a kin-oh-form: rings called Fresnel zones, about one micron thick.

segments.text: The zones narrow toward the edge, where light must bend most steeply. There, they're only a few wavelengths wide.
segments.say: The zones narrow toward the edge, where light must bend most steeply. There, they're only a few wavelengths wide.

segments.text: At the design wavelength, the kinoform multiplies the light by exactly the same e^(iφ). So it focuses to exactly the same spot.
segments.say: At the design wavelength, the kin-oh-form multiplies the light by exactly the same factor, e to the i phi. So it focuses to exactly the same spot.

segments.text: Real fabrication often makes just N discrete heights, so each zone becomes a staircase.
segments.say: Real fabrication often makes just N discrete heights, so each zone becomes a staircase.

segments.text: Each zone works like a tooth of a grating. A perfect ramp sends all the light into one diffraction order: the one aimed at the focus.
segments.say: Each zone works like a tooth of a grating. A perfect ramp sends all the light into one diffraction order: the one aimed at the focus.

segments.text: Steps leak light into other orders, and that light misses the focus.
segments.say: Steps leak light into other orders, and that light misses the focus.

segments.text: How much? At each point, draw an arrow for the gap between its phase and the perfect ramp, then add the arrows head to tail.
segments.say: How much? At each point, draw an arrow for the gap between its phase and the perfect ramp, then add the arrows, head to tail.

segments.text: For the ramp, they all line up. But each step holds its phase while the ramp keeps turning, so the chain curls, and its end-to-end arrow is shorter.
segments.say: For the ramp, they all line up. But each step holds its phase while the ramp keeps turning, so the chain curls, and its end to end arrow is shorter.

segments.text: Its squared length is the share of light in the focus: η = sinc²(1/N). That's 41% for two levels, 81% for four, 95% for eight, 99% for sixteen.
segments.say: Its squared length is the share of light in the focus: eta equals sink squared, of one over N. That's forty one percent for two levels, eighty one for four, ninety five for eight, and ninety nine for sixteen.

segments.text: Now colour. A kinoform works by diffraction: its zones are fixed, and longer wavelengths bend more at each one.
segments.say: Now, colour. A kin-oh-form works by diffraction: its zones are fixed, and longer wavelengths bend more at each one.

segments.text: So its focal length depends on colour, f = f₀λ₀/λ: red focuses closest, and blue farthest.
segments.say: So its focal length depends on colour: eff equals eff naught, lambda naught, over lambda. Red focuses closest, and blue, farthest.

segments.text: A glass lens does the opposite, and far more gently: glass bends blue slightly more, so blue focuses a little closer.
segments.say: A glass lens does the opposite, and far more gently: glass bends blue slightly more, so blue focuses a little closer.

segments.text: Opticians score this with the Abbe number: about +60 for common glass, but −3.45 for every diffractive lens.
segments.say: Opticians score this with the Ahbuh number: about plus sixty for common glass, but minus three point four five, for every diffractive lens.

segments.text: Since the signs are opposite, a weak diffractive surface can cancel a glass lens's colour error. Or software can correct the colours afterwards.
segments.say: Since the signs are opposite, a weak diffractive surface can cancel a glass lens's colour error. Or software can correct the colours afterwards.

segments.text: Now the deepest catch. The thin element approximation assumes every column of glass acts on its own. Is that true?
segments.say: Now the deepest catch. The thin element approximation assumes every column of glass acts on its own. Is that true?

segments.text: Zoom in on zones four wavelengths wide, with walls two wavelengths tall.
segments.say: Zoom in on zones four wavelengths wide, with walls two wavelengths tall.

segments.text: Solve Maxwell's equations directly, and the clean picture breaks. Light crowds along the walls, shoots out in jets, and leaves shadows beside them.
segments.say: Solve Maxwell's equations directly, and the clean picture breaks. Light crowds along the walls, shoots out in jets, and leaves shadows beside them.

segments.text: So less light reaches the focus: TEA promises all of it, but the full solution delivers about 70%.
segments.say: So less light reaches the focus: T, E, A, promises all of it, but the full solution delivers about seventy percent.

segments.text: The narrower the zones, the bigger the gap. Only zones many wavelengths wide are safe.
segments.say: The narrower the zones, the bigger the gap. Only zones many wavelengths wide are safe.

segments.text: Two ways out. Metasurfaces build the phase from pillars narrower than a wavelength, each one's delay computed from the full equations.
segments.say: Two ways out. Metasurfaces build the phase from pillars narrower than a wavelength, each one's delay computed from the full equations.

segments.text: Or drop the shortcut, and simulate the whole element with a full-wave solver. That's Episode 9.
segments.say: Or drop the shortcut, and simulate the whole element with a full wave solver. That's episode nine.

segments.text: On a computer, a flat lens takes two steps: multiply the field by e^(ik₀(n − 1)h), then propagate it with the angular spectrum method from Episode 1.
segments.say: On a computer, a flat lens takes two steps: multiply the field by e to the i, kay naught, en minus one, aitch. Then propagate it with the angular spectrum method, from episode one.

segments.text: Three pitfalls: sample the finest zone with several points, wrap the heights, and simulate the profile you can really make, not the drawing.
segments.say: Three pitfalls: sample the finest zone with several points, wrap the heights, and simulate the profile you can really make, not the drawing.

segments.text: Blur this profile by a quarter of a micron, and a quarter of the focused light is gone.
segments.say: Blur this profile by a quarter of a micron, and a quarter of the focused light is gone.

segments.text: A thin element only delays light. Phase wraps at 2π, so a lens can be a micron thick, until “thin” stops being true.
segments.say: A thin element only delays light. Phase wraps at two pi, so a lens can be a micron thick, until thin stops being true.

segments.text: The price: steps scatter light, colours split apart, and fine zones stop being thin.
segments.say: The price: steps scatter light, colours split apart, and fine zones stop being thin.

segments.text: And a lens's outer zones look a lot like a grating. So next time: what does periodic structure do to light?
segments.say: And a lens's outer zones look a lot like a grating. So next time: what does periodic structure do to light?
